title: Ops & Finance Pocket Brief — Inference Deployment Tradeoffs (2026)
body:
Overview
========
This brief is designed to be a single-stop reference for operator and finance stakeholders evaluating LLM inference deployments. It emphasizes measurable economics, concrete pilot steps, and concise security answers for procurement.

Sections
--------
- Positioning and one-line messages for buyer conversations
- Short competitive recap and scoring focused on cost and ops overhead
- Pricing guidance and concrete examples to model pilots
- A compact pitch-deck outline for meetings with Ops + Finance
- Pilot runbook and case-study summary
- Operator CLI examples and a focused security FAQ

Ownership & escalation
----------------------
- Primary owner: Go-to-market (Solutions Engineering) for pilot orchestration.
- Escalation: Engineering SRE for performance incidents; Security for compliance evidence requests.

Success criteria for pilots (example)
------------------------------------
- Observability: token-level billing export in place and validated within first 7 days.
- Economics: modeled per-session cost within 15% of projected value after caching/quantization tuning.
- Latency: p95 meets the agreed SLO for at least 95% of test windows during a 7-day soak.
- Security: KMS/certificate configuration verified and pen-test checklist passed for Private pilots.

Appendices
---------
Appendix A — Representative telemetry fields to collect:
- request_id, timestamp, route, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, GPU_util_pct, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, error_rate

Appendix B — Suggested eval metrics for finance/ops alignment:
- quality delta at quantization profile levels (none, 8-bit, 4-bit)
- effective tokens saved by prefix caching (baseline tokens vs cached tokens)
- throughput uplift from batching vs p95 latency impact

Contact
-------
For pilot support contact: priya.m@redwood.ai and the Solutions Engineering Slack channel #se-pilots.
